summary: Attacked the library audit AUDIT-02, which covers five roadmaps — HodgeStructures, JacobianChallenge, StableReduction, ArithmeticGaloisDuality and GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic — in 37 layer entries with 254 targets and 519 declaration citations. One finding, of low severity: two Mathlib declarations are cited by an unqualified name that resolves to nothing at the pin, though both exist at exactly the file and line given, under their `NumberField.Units.` prefix. Everything else held. The audit covers every stage of all five roadmaps; no citation has a wrong file, line or library tag; none is private or sorried; the library fields never contradict the citations; the four `built` verdicts survive reading the statements behind them; no `absent` target is in the libraries under another name; and the 97 recorded duplicates leave nothing obvious unrecorded.
checked: Stage coverage, the check that caught a gap in a sister audit: the audit's layer entries are exactly the stages of its five roadmaps, 4 for HodgeStructures, 6 for JacobianChallenge, 12 for StableReduction, 8 for ArithmeticGaloisDuality and 7 for GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, with nothing unaudited and nothing audited that is not a stage.

Every one of the 519 declaration citations against the pinned index (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474): none is tagged to the wrong library, none names a file the declaration is not in, and none is more than twelve lines from where the index puts it. Two names do not resolve at all, which is the finding below.
Whether any cited declaration is unusable: none of the 519 is private, and no cited declaration has a `sorry` anywhere in its body. Every cited file was opened.

Internal consistency: no target whose library field is mathlib, tauceti or both cites declarations from a different library; no target marked absent carries an exact-fit citation; and no layer marked built contains an absent or partial target.

The one apparent verdict inconsistency, which is not one. ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4 is graded 'not built' although one of its six targets is marked tauceti and another partial. The target's own note explains the grade and I accept it: the built target is the generic dual M -> N with its equivariant evaluation pairing, an upstream ProfiniteCohomology construction rather than one of this layer's duality statements, and the note says so outright — 'since none of this layer's duality statements (local invariants, global duality, the nine-term sequence, lattice versions) exists, the layer is recorded as not built'. The grading is also consistent with the rest of the audit, where six other 'not built' layers carry partial targets.

The four `built` verdicts, which are the audit's strongest claims, by reading the statements behind them rather than the names. TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.conj_piece reads `(hs.piece p).map ω.toEquiv.toLinearMap = hs.piece (n - p)`, which is the target's Hodge symmetry; isInternal_piece reads `DirectSum.IsInternal hs.piece`, which is the target verbatim; hodgeNumber_symm reads `hs.hodgeNumber p = hs.hodgeNumber (n - p)`; and Polarization.hodgeForm_self_pos reads `0 < P.hodgeForm x x` for `x ≠ 0`, which is the positive-definiteness claimed.

The one target of a `built` layer with no exact-fit citation, which looked like an over-claim and is not. 'Symmetry group Aut(V, Qint) of integral automorphisms preserving the form' is carried by TauCeti.BilinForm.isometryGroup with fit 'more general', and reading it settles the question: it is the subgroup of linear equivalences preserving an arbitrary bilinear form over a commutative ring, and its own docstring says 'For a finite free `ℤ`-module `V` carrying an integral form `Q` this is the arithmetic group `Aut(V, Q)`'. The audit's note says the same.

The 157 targets marked absent, for mathematics the libraries have under another name. The deep algebraic geometry is genuinely absent: searching the pinned index finds nothing for the theorem of the cube, the dual abelian variety, the Picard functor or scheme, Abel-Jacobi maps, symmetric powers of a curve as schemes, Cech cohomology, dualizing sheaves and complexes, higher direct images, or cohomology and base change.

Duplication, recorded and unrecorded. The audit records 97 duplicate entries across its 37 layers, each naming a specific other layer. I swept every roadmap in the atlas for the six concepts most likely to be planned twice here — stable curves and maps, the Picard functor, abelian varieties, dualizing sheaves, Hodge structures and the geometry of numbers — and found nothing the audit misses. The nearest candidates were the three roadmaps outside the audit that mention Hodge structures where the audit records only AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A5, and all three consume rather than duplicate: ShimuraData:D1 names 'the HodgeStructures linear-algebraic API' among its dependencies, PELModuli:M0 relates its positivity condition 'to the associated Hodge structure', and ShimuraCompactifications:C1 takes the mixed Hodge structure it needs at a boundary.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-02.result.json, roadmap GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, layer GN.1, the target 'Unit application: Dirichlet's unit theorem via convex bodies' — its citations `finrank_modTorsion` and `exist_unique_eq_mul_prod`
findings.claim: Two of the audit's 519 declaration citations name a Mathlib declaration by an unqualified name that exists under no such name at the pin. Both declarations are real and are at exactly the file and line the audit gives, but their names are NumberField.Units.finrank_modTorsion and NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod, and the audit drops the namespace. A consumer of data/library-coverage.json who resolves a citation by its `name` — which is how the coverage record is meant to be used — finds nothing for these two, while the other 517 resolve. The mathematical claim behind the target, that Mathlib has Dirichlet's unit theorem, is correct and is not in question.
findings.evidence: The audit's two citations read name 'finrank_modTorsion', library mathlib, file Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean, line 457, fit exact; and name 'exist_unique_eq_mul_prod', same file, line 506, fit exact. At the pin that file declares 'theorem finrank_modTorsion : finrank ℤ (Additive ((𝓞 K)ˣ ⧸ (torsion K))) = rank K' at line 457 and 'theorem exist_unique_eq_mul_prod (x : (𝓞 K)ˣ) : ∃! ζe : torsion K × (Fin (rank K) → ℤ), ...' at line 506, and the declarations index records them as NumberField.Units.finrank_modTorsion and NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod at those same lines. Looking either bare name up in the index returns nothing. The rest of the audit is qualified correctly: of the 519 citations these two are the only ones that fail to resolve, and the audit's other Mathlib citations in the same layer, for instance NumberField.mixedEmbedding.volume_fundamentalDomain_stdBasis and ZLattice.covolume_eq_det, carry their full namespaces. Note that this is the opposite of the failure mode that looks similar and is not a defect, where the index itself drops a namespace and the audit's name is the correct one; here the index has the full name and the audit has the short one.
findings.fix: Rewrite the two `name` fields as NumberField.Units.finrank_modTorsion and NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod, leaving the file, line, library and fit fields as they are, and carry the corrected names into the AUDIT-02 entry for GN.1 when it is merged into data/library-coverage.json. Nothing else in the target or the layer changes: both citations are exact fits for the Dirichlet unit theorem target and remain so.
